content: The greatest obstacle to living is expectancy, which hangs upon tomorrow and loses today.
author: Seneca
story:
Rather than offering a polite platitude, this observation challenges how we navigate our inner lives. Most human unhappiness exists in two places that don't currently exist: the past, which cannot be changed, and the future, which hasn't happened yet. Meanwhile, the only life you will ever experience is slipping past unnoticed.

Across his life and work, Seneca saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Presence is not a rare mystical achievement; it is simply having the courtesy to show up for your own life. When you anchor your awareness in the immediate room and task, the frantic anxieties of the ego dissolve.
reflectionPrompt: How can you integrate the essence of this wisdom into one specific decision or encounter today?
